trust_boundaries: external-to-ingestion: data_sources to kafka_cluster (mixed trust — some sources untrusted)
processing-to-storage: spark_cluster to data_lake and data_warehouse
storage-to-analytics: data_lake/data_warehouse to ml_models and bi_dashboard
architecture_summary.operational_context: Multi-cloud streaming data pipeline from external sources through Kafka/Spark to analytics

threat_actors.name: Compromised Data Source
threat_actors.motivation: Data poisoning — inject manipulated records to corrupt downstream analytics and ML models
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Compromise of one of the external data source connectors feeding Kafka
non_capabilities: No direct access to Spark, data lake, or data warehouse
No ability to modify ML model weights directly
No access to BI dashboard configuration

threat_actors.name: Insider Data Analyst
threat_actors.motivation: Exfiltrate sensitive datasets from data warehouse for competitive intelligence
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate BI dashboard credentials with query access to data warehouse
non_capabilities: No direct data lake object storage access — only through BI layer

threat_actors.name: External Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Access sensitive data at rest in data lake or warehouse
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Misconfigured storage bucket or exposed Spark UI
non_capabilities: No valid credentials for any tier
No network access without exploiting a public-facing component first

attack_paths.entry_point: Kafka broker port or management UI exposed to external data source network
attack_paths.impact: Unauthorized topic access or message injection into pipeline
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Kafka clusters commonly misconfigured with no authentication on internal segments exposed to producer networks

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious Spark job submitted via compromised Kafka message or API
attack_paths.impact: Code execution on Spark cluster nodes, access to all data transiting through processing layer
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Spark arbitrary code execution via job submission is a known attack vector; cluster API often insufficiently protected

attack_paths.entry_point: Spark job with write permissions to data lake (AP-002)
attack_paths.impact: Deletion or overwrite of raw data in data lake, causing analytics pipeline failure
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires AP-002 success; Spark jobs typically have scoped write permissions but rarely least-privilege

attack_paths.entry_point: Over-privileged BI dashboard query interface or direct JDBC access
attack_paths.impact: Mass export of aggregated sensitive records from data warehouse
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: BI tools frequently allow bulk export; data warehouse access controls often permissive for analyst usability

attack_paths.entry_point: Cryptomining payload injected via malicious Spark job
attack_paths.impact: Cluster resource exhaustion causing pipeline SLA breaches
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Large compute clusters are high-value cryptomining targets; impact is operational rather than data-focused

attack_paths.entry_point: Poisoned training data injected via compromised data source (AP-001)
attack_paths.impact: Model output manipulation — adversarial data skews ML predictions affecting business decisions
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Data poisoning requires sustained injection over multiple pipeline runs to affect model training

attack_paths.entry_point: Stolen analyst credentials used to run ad-hoc export queries
attack_paths.impact: Authorised but unauthorised-intent bulk data export
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Analyst credentials are high-value; credential theft via phishing is common for privileged technical users

attack_paths.entry_point: Disabling audit logging on Kafka broker via admin API compromise
attack_paths.impact: Removes visibility into message injection attacks, allowing sustained data poisoning undetected
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires admin-level Kafka access; high impact to detection but harder to achieve

mitigations.control_name: Kafka SASL/TLS authentication and ACL-based topic access control
Spark job signing and submission whitelist
Immutable data lake with versioning and object-lock
DLP monitoring on BI export operations
Spark cluster resource quotas and job isolation
Training data provenance tracking and anomaly detection
MFA for analyst accounts accessing data warehouse
Kafka audit log immutability and offsite shipping

findings.severity_rationale: Spark cluster without job signing allows arbitrary code execution across entire processing layer with data lake write access
Bulk export from data warehouse via BI tool is possible without DLP; restricted data at scale
Kafka authentication gap allows message injection from compromised data source network
Data poisoning through compromised source is low probability per run but cumulative effect on ML models is significant over time
Data lake destruction requires AP-002 first; object lock mitigates to recoverable impact
Resource hijacking for cryptomining is mitigated by existing resource quotas; availability impact only
Audit log tampering is already mitigated by immutable offsite shipping; residual risk is negligible
